clue.text: Old boats chase fish; they're probably full at 8

indicators.note: to chase is to follow behind, so the boats come after the fish

parts.note: the carp is a freshwater fish
arks, like Noah's, are old-fashioned boats

explanation.surface: Ancient vessels pursue a fish, and somewhere is crowded at a place numbered 8.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue 8 is SANDWICH, the Kent town whose golf course was hosting the Open championship that week, so its parking areas would be packed with spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaces for vehicles fill up when a big golf tournament draws crowds to a small town.

clue.text: PM in European country left bottom out

indicators.note: the bottom left of a map is south-west, so those two compass letters are taken out of the country

parts.note: Sweden is a Scandinavian nation

explanation.surface: A prime minister from abroad left with his backside exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left bottom' is the south-west corner on a compass, and 'out' removes it from the country's name, leaving the surname of the 1950s prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Eden was a British prime minister in the 1950s, so the abbreviation for premier fits him.

clue.text: Oversaw fabric turnover (clothes department)

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here, the flipped fabric dressing round the abbreviation
turnover asks for the fabric word to be flipped end to end

parts.note: denim is the cotton cloth of jeans

explanation.surface: Someone supervised the stock rotation of cloth in the clothing section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' makes MINED from DENIM; 'clothes' wraps that round D, giving MIN-D-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have minded something is to have looked after or supervised it.

clue.text: Why Eisenhower got drunk downing his third rye, perhaps

indicators.note: downing as swallowing a drink, the scrambled letters taking in another one
got drunk suggests letters reeling about into a new order

parts.note: why taken as written, plus Ike, the nickname of US President Dwight Eisenhower

indicators.note: third picks the third letter of the word his

explanation.surface: A question about why the US president became intoxicated after swallowing a rye.
explanation.walkthrough: Ike was Eisenhower's nickname, so this is an indirect anagram; 'downing' has the jumbled letters swallow the third letter of 'his'. The -EY spelling is the American and Irish one, apt for an American president.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is an American style of spirit distilled from grain, one example of this drink.

clue.text: Trim sprawling Cupressus outside Sunday school, quietly

indicators.note: sprawling suggests the remaining letters spread out in a new arrangement
outside in the sense of 'put out', the two letters being expelled from the tree's name

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: A gardener tidies an overgrown cypress beside a Sunday school, doing it silently.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S and S from CUPRESSUS ('outside') to leave CUPREUS, rearrange ('sprawling') to SPRUCEU, and add P.
explanation.definitionFit: To smarten up or tidy something is to trim it into shape.

clue.text: One of 26 is situated over at west end of Med, opening up Arles

indicators.note: the west end of a word written left to right is its first letter
opening up means the town's name is prised apart to admit the other letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: over means the word for being situated is read backwards

parts.note: something that is situated somewhere lies there

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean port sits at the western edge of the sea, opening up the route to Arles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses the word for situated, and 'opening up' prises the French town apart to take it in. Clue 26 is SEAPORTS; the English spelling keeps a final S the French name lacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Marseilles is France's great Mediterranean harbour city, an example of a coastal port.

clue.text: 10 performing in nude, shivering

indicators.note: in says the performing word goes inside the jumbled letters
shivering suggests the letters trembling into a new order

parts.note: a show that is on is being performed

explanation.surface: Someone is acting naked and shaking with cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shivering' rearranges NUDE to UNDE, and ON goes 'in' to make UND-ON-E. Clue 10 is OPEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A shirt left unbuttoned is open, so not fastened works as a synonym.

clue.text: This week's 10 course sold by 22 down

explanation.surface: A golf venue this week whose name is also something on sale at a fast-food chain.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal St George's at Sandwich in Kent hosted the 2011 Open golf championship; Subway (22 down) is a sandwich chain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kent town hosted the golf championship that year, and the chain sells filled rolls and bread snacks.

clue.text: Man on board eats right sort of 8

indicators.note: eats means the chessman's word takes the letter inside it

parts.note: a pawn is a chess piece, a man on the chessboard

explanation.surface: A crew member on a ship consumes the correct kind of snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' looks like a sailor, but the board is a chessboard. Clue 8 is SANDWICH, so this is a filling.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafood filling with mayonnaise makes a popular kind of lunchtime bread snack.

clue.text: Frank's in gym regularly taking hooks

indicators.note: in signals one part placed within the other
hooks as grabbing hold of, the taking word holding the gym letters

parts.note: someone regularly taking a medicine is on it
PE, physical education, is school gym

explanation.surface: A man called Frank goes to the gym regularly and learns to throw punches.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a man's name; it means candid. 'Regularly taking' a drug is being on it, and 'in' plus 'hooks' both describe gym held within.
explanation.definitionFit: Being candid and honest means being straightforward, without anything hidden.

clue.text: Talk in field event is about leg

parts.note: the discus is a throwing event in athletics

indicators.note: about means the little word is turned round

parts.note: the leg side in cricket is also called the on side

explanation.surface: Discussion at an athletics event concerns a leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses IS to SI. In cricket the leg side is also known as the on side, so 'leg' gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A discussion is a conversation in which views are exchanged.

clue.text: Polished golfer's beginning 18 holes

indicators.note: beginning takes the first letter of the word golfer's

parts.note: a round of golf is eighteen holes

explanation.surface: A slick golfer starts a full round of the course.
explanation.definitionFit: A lens is ground to polish it smooth, so smoothed by abrasion is the sense.

clue.text: It could be intrusive at Yankee campus

indicators.note: could be says these letters could be rearranged into something else

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A remark that something might be invasive at an American college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges the word intrusive, and the phonetic-alphabet Yankee supplies the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the grounds of a college, standing here for the institution itself.

clue.text: Survey ship: it's laid on to bring out pupils

definitions.text: it's laid on to bring out pupils

parts.note: to eye something is to survey it
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A survey vessel apparently lays something on to bring schoolchildren out.
explanation.walkthrough: The pupils are the dark centres of the eyes, not schoolchildren; makeup is laid on to make them stand out.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetics drawn round the eye make it look more striking, highlighting the iris and pupil.

clue.text: It's able to be composted for saxifrage

indicators.note: composting breaks material down and mixes it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, with its S
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener claims a plant can go on the compost heap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be composted' rearranges ITS + ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Astilbe is a feathery flowering perennial in the saxifrage family of plants.

clue.text: They support British business at Gravesend

parts.note: a racket is a business, especially a dodgy one
read as Graves end, the end of Graves, its last letter

explanation.surface: Commercial firms in the Kent town of Gravesend get support.
explanation.walkthrough: Gravesend is a town in Kent, but it is split as 'Graves end'. Wall supports for shelves are also called this.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelf supports fixed to a wall are angle pieces holding things up.

clue.text: Poor example of a heartless guy bagging game

indicators.note: bagging means catching, so the outer letters capture the game
heartless removes the middle of the word guy, leaving its outsides

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: A sorry specimen of a man without feeling catches some sport.
explanation.walkthrough: A + GY ('heartless guy') bag POLO: A-POLO-GY. 'An apology for a meal' means a poor example of one.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling something a sorry excuse for its kind is the idiomatic sense of a wretched specimen.

clue.text: Somersaulting over 13 they could get nystagmus

definitions.text: Somersaulting over 13 they could get nystagmus

indicators.note: somersaulting tumbles the letters of the eye condition into a new order

parts.note: 13 down is UNIVERSITY, and U is its usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: People turning somersaults might develop an eye condition involving involuntary movement.
explanation.walkthrough: NYSTAGMUS rearranged ('Somersaulting') with U, from 13 down, taken 'over' or removed, gives the answer. Nystagmus is a rapid involuntary eye movement, linked with dizziness.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumbling athletes spin repeatedly, which can upset the eyes and balance.

clue.text: Wordy half of book's boring poems

indicators.note: boring as drilling into, so the half word goes inside the poems

parts.note: verse is poetry

indicators.note: half of takes the first two of the four letters

explanation.surface: Half of a long-winded book consists of dull poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: BO, 'half of book', bores into VERSE: VER-BO-SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Using more words than needed is long-winded, a direct synonym.

clue.text: It's plain he'd mistakenly held a note over

indicators.note: held means the scrambled letters hold the turned phrase
mistakenly says these letters are put in the wrong order
over reverses the phrase of the article plus the note word

parts.note: a memo is a short written note

explanation.surface: A man insists something is simple after wrongly keeping a written note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistakenly' turns HE'D into H..DE; 'over' reverses A MEMO to OMEMA, which those letters 'held'.
explanation.definitionFit: Home-produced food or goods are plain and simple, without professional finish.

clue.text: School underperforming? It's authority's point of view

parts.note: read as under performing: performing gives ON, and the school word goes under it in the down light
a high school is a secondary school

explanation.surface: A school doing badly asks whether that is how the authorities see it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underperforming' looks like doing badly; split it as 'under performing', so the school word sits beneath the performing word in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Orders from above come from people in power, the viewpoint of those at the top.

clue.text: Source of oil raises a Mexican's holding

indicators.note: holding means these words contain the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A Mexican's property increases in value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' looks like property, but it signals the letters held inside 'raiSES A MExican's'.
explanation.definitionFit: The seeds of this plant are pressed for a cooking oil used widely in Asian food.

clue.text: Power governs tube centrally — US tube, that is

indicators.note: governs as in holding sway over, the power word surrounding the middle letters

parts.note: sway is power or influence

indicators.note: centrally takes the middle letters of the word tube

explanation.surface: Electricity controls the middle of a tube line in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centrally' gives UB, which SWAY surrounds ('governs'). An American metro is called this, matching British 'tube'.
explanation.definitionFit: The American name for an underground railway corresponds to the London tube.

clue.text: A sheikh's B&B barbecued food for him?

definitions.text: A sheikh's B&B barbecued food for him?

indicators.note: barbecued suggests the letters are cooked up into a new form

parts.note: the S of the possessive is counted here
the letters B and B of the abbreviation

explanation.surface: A sheikh's bed and breakfast cooks grilled food for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barbecued' rearranges A SHEIKHS BB. The whole clue also describes the dish: grilled meat suitable for an Arab sheikh.
explanation.definitionFit: Skewered grilled meat of Middle Eastern origin is just what a sheikh might eat.

clue.text: International leaves perfect wood not far from 8

indicators.note: leaves means the letter goes away from the word for perfect

parts.note: ideal means perfect

explanation.surface: An international player walks out of the perfect forest near a Kent town.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions run together: pine timber, and the Kent town about six miles from SANDWICH (8).
explanation.definitionFit: This word is pine or fir timber and also a Kent coastal town close to Sandwich.

clue.text: Anonymous donor makes an entrance

indicators.note: anonymous means without a name, and N abbreviates name, so that letter goes

explanation.surface: A benefactor who stays unnamed arrives on the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes an entrance' looks like an arrival; the definition is the doorway itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorway is the way in to a room or building.

clue.text: Bribe Gulf State for Sarkozy

parts.note: G abbreviates Gulf
the French word for state is etat, and Nicolas Sarkozy was the French president

explanation.surface: Someone bribes a Gulf state on behalf of the French president.
explanation.definitionFit: To get at someone is an idiom for corrupting or influencing them improperly.

clue.text: Each displays nets in harbours

indicators.note: nets as catching, the word for displays capturing the abbreviation

parts.note: to sport something is to display it, as in sporting a tie

explanation.surface: Each fisherman shows off his nets in the ports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nets' looks like fishing gear but means catches: S-EA-PORTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Coastal towns with docks are places where ships shelter and unload.
